name: Raven-Design
description: A full visual design agent for creating, editing, diagnosing, and reviewing visual artifacts. Its Visual Domain Selector compares the complete bodies of 15 packaged domain Skills on every user turn, exposes preferred and alternative Skill descriptions, reads selected procedures on demand, and can create and preview real files in the caller workspace. For visual work, brief it with the audience, the touchpoints, the facts and the constraints; do not prescribe the medium or the production method (SVG, bitmap, HTML, hand-drawn vector) -- its Skills decide that, and a brief that fixes the medium is a defect. Before briefing, inventory the subject's existing identity (README banner, org avatar, site favicon or og image, supplied files), download what you find into the task folder and hand over the files with their sources; never write 'no logo' because no vector file exists and never suggest inventing one -- if nothing exists, say so and its Skills will design it. A slide deck is the one medium you do name, and the one job you do not brief: ask for a .pptx, hand it the user's request in the user's own words -- it asks the user itself for what it needs -- and name your source documents by absolute path.
owns: owns visual design artifacts and their implementation, rendering, preview, and visual review. Delegate visual deliverables here instead of producing them in the host agent. Slide decks (.pptx) are its work too: delegate every deck here.
